description:
Found by an s423 (#418) review probe, and PRE-EXISTING for ASCII names too —
the non-ASCII case behaves exactly like the ASCII one, which is why it did not
block #418.

    package Foo;
    sub where { 1 }
    our $y = 7;
    our @w = (1);
    package main;
    print join(",", sort keys %Foo::), "\n";
    # perl: w,where,y      PCL: where

`p-stash` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, ~line 7590) walks `do-symbols` over the CL
package and keeps only the symbols whose name carries the `pl-` sub prefix, so
a package's SCALAR/ARRAY/HASH globals never appear as stash keys — and
`exists $Foo::{y}` / `delete $Foo::{y}` answer on that same snapshot.

The utf8 twin is identical (`our $ｙ` in `package ＦＯＯ` is missing from
`keys %ＦＯＯ::` the same way), so this is ONE bug, not two: #418 made the
non-ASCII case behave exactly like the ASCII case, and this is what both do.

Fix shape: the stash snapshot has to include the sigil-prefixed variable
symbols under their perl NAME (perl's stash keys are the bare name).  The
design question the task carries: perl's stash VALUE is a GLOB, and PCL's
stash values are code-ref boxes — `docs/ir-spec.md` has no glob-valued stash.
Measure what the corpus actually does with a stash key before choosing
(t/uni/stash.t is the population).

Reproducer: the six-line program above.  `Pl/t/utf8-source-01.t` row
'PACKAGE: p-defpackage and p-stash agree on a fullwidth name (#418)' asserts
the SUB half only, deliberately.


s425 (Fable review probe): a SECOND spelling of the same snapshot â perl VIVIFIES a stash entry on a FAILED method lookup, so `Foo->can("nope"); exists $Foo::{nope}` prints 1 in perl and 0 in PCL (ASCII-identical, pre-existing, perl-internals class; record it here rather than in a new task).
title: keys %Pkg:: lists only SUBS — package VARIABLES are missing from the stash
